# Jane Andrews

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c6 P4](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0004), [v1 c11 P18](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0018)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c11 P18](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0018), [v1 c33 P6](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0006)</sub>
- **Role:** Schoolteacher  <sub>[v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Jane is described as plain, wholesome, pink, and sweet. She is compared in appearance to an apple blossom.

_Sources: [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v2 c13 P70](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0070)_

## Personality

Jane is composed, steady, sensible, and practical. She is conscientious, plodding, and lacks imagination, preferring straightforward facts over poetic or romantic ideas. She is generally calm under pressure and not easily rattled during examinations.

_Sources: [v1 c31 P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 c32 P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c36 P0](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0000), [v2 c4 P8](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0008), [v2 c13 P38](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0038), [v2 c13 P72](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0072), [v2 c26 P60](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0060)_

- Schoolteaching  <sub>[v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000), [v2 c28 P3](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0003)</sub>

## Goals

- Earn her salary, please school trustees, and earn a place on the School Inspector's roll of honor  <sub>[v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002)</sub>

## History

Jane grew up in Avonlea as part of the Andrews family and attended the local school under Mr. Phillips and later Miss Stacy. She joined Anne Shirley's story club, though she preferred writing sensible stories without romance. Jane joined the Queen's class, passed her Entrance examination calmly, and completed her studies at Queen's Academy, earning honors in domestic science. After graduating, she accepted a position as a teacher in Newbridge, where she maintained order strictly and earned a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor. She active participated in the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, serving on fundraising and petition committees. After her successful term at Newbridge, she was tipped to take over the school in Avonlea.

_Sources: [v1 c11 P18](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0018), [v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c26 P20](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0020), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c32 P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002), [v2 c6 P10](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0010), [v2 c14 P49](../source/v02-c14.md#nw-v02-c14-p0049), [v2 c26 P35](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0035), [v2 c28 P3](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0003)_

- Nearly fell overboard into the Lake of Shining Waters while picking water lilies  <sub>[v1 c14 P68](../source/v01-c14.md#nw-v01-c14-p0068)</sub>
- Studied at Queen's Academy and earned honors in domestic science  <sub>[v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)</sub>
- Taught at the Newbridge school before being considered for Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000), [v2 c26 P35](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0035), [v2 c28 P3](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0003)</sub>

## Quotes

> Of course it would be romantic, but I know I couldn’t keep still. I’d be popping up every minute or so to see where I was and if I wasn’t drifting too far out. And you know, Anne, that would spoil the effect.  <sub>[v1 c28 P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002)</sub>

> I’ve a compliment for you, Anne. At least I think it must be a compliment because of the tone he said it in. Part of it was anyhow. There was an American sitting behind Jane and me—such a romantic-looking man, with coal-black hair and eyes. Josie Pye says he is a distinguished artist, and that her mother’s cousin in Boston is married to a man that used to go to school with him. Well, we heard him say—didn’t we, Jane?—‘Who is that girl on the platform with the splendid Titian hair? She has a face I should like to paint.’ There now, Anne. But what does Titian hair mean?  <sub>[v1 c33 P43](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0043)</sub>

> Give them a good whipping, of course.  <sub>[v2 c4 P4](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0004)</sub>

> Indeed, I could and would, if they deserved it,  <sub>[v2 c4 P6](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0006)</sub>

> I should rather call it a picture. A poem is lines and verses.  <sub>[v2 c13 P65](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0065)</sub>
